content.comment_body: Hello, I am new to using [product_name], but I have many years of experience with PLCs, including older models. My issue is that I cannot physically connect the [product_name] (AM2 AQ, [article_no]) to the [product_name] (version_no, [article_no]). The top encoding pin does not align properly to slide into the corresponding hole on the side of the [product_name] module. I've checked manuals and searched online, and while I see many images of the modules side-by-side, for some reason this module does not fit as expected. Is the AM2 AQ module ([article_no]) designed for [product_name] [version_no] and not [product_name] [version_no]? Thank you for your assistance.

With the release of [product_name] [version_no], completely new hardware became available. Basic modules of version 8 are not compatible with expansion modules from earlier versions. Similarly, extension modules from series 8 do not work with basic modules from previous versions (0 to 7). Expansion module order numbers from series 8 always end with [article_no], except for TDE, which ends with [article_no].

Alright, thanks; I suspected that might be the situation. Where did you find this information? I could not locate it anywhere. So, I need to use the AM2 AQ module ([article_no]) to connect to the [product_name] ([version_no], [article_no])?
Check on the manufacturer's website for details: [url] Yes, that is correct.
Thank you for sharing your expertise.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered an issue with hardware compatibility when trying to connect a newer expansion module ([product_name], [version_no], [article_no]) to an older basic module ([product_name], [version_no], [article_no]). The encoding pin design blocks physical connection between different versions. Incomplete compatibility information in manuals or official documentation creates confusion and increases the chance of buying incompatible modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear and accessible guidance on version and physical compatibility between basic and expansion modules, aiming to avoid issues with incorrectly purchased hardware.
